South Africa vs Australia, third Test: Centuries by Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder lift hosts back into series contention in Newlands decider
Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder strike centuries as South Africa set Australia 288 to win third Test and seal series victory; series winners take top spot in Test rankings; watch final day live on Sky Sports Cricket from 8am on Saturday
Friday 30 October 2026 17:49, UK
Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder struck centuries as South Africa were bowled out for 387 to close day four of the decisive third Test against Australia, setting the touring side a victory target of 288 on the final day.
Australia toiled, taking a single wicket in the opening two sessions before a burst after tea, but it was still very much the home side's day and sets up an intriguing tussle on Saturday.
Mulder top-scored with 115, his fourth Test century, while Rickelton amassed 101 as the pair ensured Australia will need to complete the second-highest successful run chase in 137 years of Test cricket at Newlands.

"It was about trying to win the small moments," Rickelton said. "We knew we were effectively 40 for four this morning and that Australia would come hard at us.
"It was about spending time at the crease rather than worrying about scoring runs or getting too far ahead of ourselves. We had our plans and needed to stick to them.
"We knew the longer we batted, the more frustrated Australia would become. Perhaps they expected things to happen quite quickly because of the deteriorating wicket."
The pitch is starting to show signs of wear, with Australia batter Josh Inglis saying on Thursday a chase of over 200 would be a difficult one batting last.
They will need considerably more than that at more than three runs an over against a South African bowling attack that has had its feet up for more than a day and a half.
South Africa resumed on the fourth morning at 140-4 and lost only Matthew Breetzke (43) in two sessions as he fell to a pull shot off Pat Cummins (2-71) and was caught on the boundary by Mitchell Starc, a familiar mode of dismissal for the home side this Test.
Rickelton and Mulder put on 154 for the sixth wicket as they took few risks and accumulated runs.
There was considerable turn for spinner Nathan Lyon (2-101) and variable bounce for the seamers.
Mulder was the last man out as he tried to up the tempo, caught on the boundary - again by Starc off Cummins - to bring a close to the day.
The series is level at 1-1 after Australia won the first Test by 214 runs in Durban and South Africa responded with a victory by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha.
"It's been a special series. It's ebbed and flowed across all three games," Rickelton added. "Both teams have got ahead at different stages, only for the other to fight back. There have been mistakes and some really good cricket as well.
"Hopefully it comes down to a really good day for South Africa tomorrow."
The winners of the match will occupy the No 1 spot in the Test world rankings, which is currently held by Australia.

digest_he:
שחקני הנבחרת דרום אפריקה, ראיין ריקלטון ווויאן מולדר, רשמו מאות מרשימות ביום הרביעי של משחק המבחן השלישי והמכריע נגד אוסטרליה בקייפטאון. המארחים נפסלו על סך של 387 ריצות, ובכך קבעו ליריבתם יעד של 288 ריצות לניצחון ביום האחרון של ההתמודדות.

מולדר הוביל את קלעי הנבחרת עם 115 ריצות וריקלטון הוסיף 101, במהלך שהציב בפני האוסטרלים את אחד האתגרים הקשים ביותר במגרש זה בהיסטוריה של משחקי המבחן. המנצחת בסדרה המאוזנת תטפס למקום הראשון בדירוג העולמי בענף הקריקט.
